props.gloss_en: the mishna: [a stove heated] with pomace or wood -- he may not place [it] until he sweeps or puts ash
Beit Shammai: hot water, but not a cooked dish
Beit Hillel: hot water and a cooked dish
Beit Shammai: one may remove, but not return
Beit Hillel: one may even return
horn 1: the mishna's 'he may not place' means he may not RETURN [a pot]
horn 1: but to LEAVE [a pot] -- one may leave it, even though [the stove] is not swept and not covered
horn 1: and whose is [the mishna]? Chananya's
Chananya: whatever is [cooked] like the food of ben Drosai may be left on a stove, even though it is not swept and not covered
horn 2: or perhaps the mishna taught [that one may not] LEAVE [a pot]
horn 2: if swept and covered, yes; if not, no -- and all the more so [not] to return
Rav: they taught [permission] only on top of [the stove], but inside it is forbidden
two adjoining stoves, one swept and covered and one not -- one may leave [a pot] on the swept and covered one
and one may not leave [a pot] on the one that is not swept and not covered
R' Meir's version: what may one leave? Beit Shammai: nothing at all
[what may be left:] hot water, but not a cooked dish -- BH in R' Meir's version, BS in R' Yehuda's
R' Meir's version: if he removed [it], all agree he may not return it
R' Yehuda's version: Beit Hillel -- hot water and a cooked dish [may be left]
horn 1 (and the resolution at 37a.10): inside and on top of [an unswept stove] are forbidden, but leaning [a pot] against it is fine
horn 2: or perhaps [leaning] is no different -- forbidden
Rav Chiyya: [a stove] he covered and that flared up -- one leans [a pot] against it, leaves [one] on it, removes from it and returns to it
a stove heated with pomace or wood -- one may lean [a pot] against it
and one may not leave [a pot on it] unless it is swept and covered
coals that dimmed -- it is as [a stove that is] covered
or [a stove] on which he put fine flax chaff -- it is as [one that is] covered
Rav Oshaya: [a stove] he covered and that reignited -- one may leave on it hot water fully heated and a dish fully cooked
[food that] shrivels and improves [may be left] -- inferred by the stam at 37b.1-2 (rejected), stated by R' Yochanan via Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda at 37b.5
R' Yochanan: [a stove] covered and reignited -- one may leave fully heated water and fully cooked food on it, even [if its] coals are of broom-wood
R' Yochanan (Rav Sheshet): a stove heated with pomace or wood -- one may leave on it hot water not fully heated and a dish not fully cooked
R' Yochanan (Rav Sheshet): if he removed [it], he may not return it until he sweeps or puts ash
the mishna [Rava quotes]: one may not put bread into the oven at nightfall, nor a cake on coals, unless [there is time] for its surface to crust
Rava: so if its surface crusted, [leaving it] is permitted
Rava: Beit Hillel permitted [returning] only on a swept and covered [stove], not on one unswept
[food that] shrivels and improves -- [leaving it] is forbidden
Rav Ukva of Meishan: you, who are close to Rav and Shmuel, do as Rav and Shmuel
Rav Ukva of Meishan: we will do as R' Yochanan
Abaye's question: is it permitted to leave [food on the stove]? -- answered yes by Rav Yosef (בסורא משהו)
Rav Yosef: they leave [food] for Rav Yehuda and he eats
Abaye: except Rav Yehuda -- since he is in danger, even on Shabbat it is permitted to make [food] for him
Rav Yosef: in Sura they leave [food], for Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak, a master of [meticulous] deeds, had it left for him and ate
Rav Ashi: I stood before Rav Huna, and they left a dish of kasa deharsena for him and he ate
Rav Ashi: I do not know whether [it was] because he holds that shrivels-and-improves is permitted
Rav Ashi: or because, since it has micha in it, it shrivels and worsens
[food that] shrivels and worsens -- [leaving it] is permitted
the general rule: anything that has micha in it shrivels and worsens
except a turnip dish, which, though it has micha, shrivels and improves -- when it has meat and is not wanted for guests
but [a turnip dish] without meat shrivels and worsens
but [a turnip dish with meat] wanted for guests shrivels and worsens
lafda, porridge and dates shrivel and worsen
R' Chiyya bar Abba: one who cooks on Shabbat unwittingly may eat [it]
R' Chiyya bar Abba: deliberately -- he may not eat
R' Chiyya bar Abba: 'and it is no different' -- [one who forgot a pot on the stove is] no different [from one who cooks]
Rabba and Rav Yosef: 'no different' is permissive -- the one who did no act [of cooking] may eat even if [he left it] deliberately
Rabba and Rav Yosef: it is the cook, who performs an act, who may not eat when [he acted] deliberately
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: 'no different' is restrictive -- the one [who forgot] may not eat even if unwittingly
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: it is the cook who will not come to act deceitfully [who may eat when unwitting]; this one may come to deceive
the baraita (R' Meir): one forgot a pot on a stove and it cooked on Shabbat -- unwittingly, he may eat; this is said of water not fully heated and food not fully cooked
the baraita (R' Meir): deliberately -- he may not eat
R' Meir: but water fully heated and food fully cooked -- whether unwittingly or deliberately, he may eat
R' Yehuda: fully heated water is permitted, because it shrivels and worsens

R' Yehuda: a fully cooked dish is forbidden, because it shrivels and improves (and so everything that shrivels and improves, e.g. cabbage, beans and minced meat, is forbidden; what shrivels and worsens is permitted)
for Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: here [the baraita] is before the decree, there [his reading] after the decree
Rav: at first they would say: one who cooks on Shabbat -- unwittingly eats, deliberately not; and the same holds for one who forgets
Rav: when those who leave deliberately and say 'we forgot' multiplied, they went back and penalized the one who forgets
horn 1: one who transgressed and left [a pot] -- did the Sages penalize him [and forbid it]?
horn 2: or not
R' Yosei found hot water that had been left on a stove and did not forbid it to them
[he found] shriveled eggs that had been left on a stove, and forbade them to them
so shriveled eggs are [food that] shrivels and improves? -- yes
Rav Chama bar Chanina: once Rebbi and I were guests somewhere, and they brought us eggs shriveled like crab-apples, and we ate many of them
